School & learning

subjunctive noun and adjective

the mood

also subjunctive mood, in the subjunctive, conjunctive

late Latin

Diom. p. 331 P.; Prisc. p. 820 P. (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 225, 249

subjūnctīvus, subjūnctīva, subjūnctīvum

declension

subjunctive; as a noun (modus understood), the subjunctive

The later grammarians’ term, from subjungere, to join on beneath: the mood of subordinate clauses. modus subjūnctīvus, the subjunctive mood; modō subjūnctīvō, in the subjunctive (Traupman 228). We have found no classical name for it.

Other words

  • conjūnctīvus, conjūnctīva, conjūnctīvum — conjunctive, subjunctive

    declension · also used · late Latin · Mart. Cap. 3.310 (Lewis & Short)

    Martianus Capella’s name, kept in some modern grammars.

Examples

  • Dā dēclīnātiōnem ejusdem verbī āctīvī, tempore praesentī, modō subjūnctīvō, singulāriter.

    Give the conjugation of the same active verb in the present subjunctive singular.Traupman 228

See also mood, indicative.

SourcesLewis & Short: subjunctivus · Lewis & Short: conjunctivus
